messages:
Priya: Seeing a spike in inter-pod retries for model-serving svc in eu-west-1, GPUs reporting backend timeouts and heavy tail latency. noticed ~20% 5xx on calls routed to nodepool-gpu-b
Alex: :eyes: timeline? config change? autoscaler activity?
Priya: started ~08:24 UTC, coincides with a burst of jobs from experiments queue + a node reboot in nodepool-gpu-b-3. No config changes pushed.
Jordan: any packet loss or MTU drops? RDMA enabled on that pool recently.
Priya: running quick pings between pods now, results look noisy. putting recent tcpdump and ipvs dump below
Priya: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
TCP  10.4.12.20:443 rr
  -> 10.2.5.21:443             Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.2.5.22:443             Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.3.7.19:443             Masq    1      0          1200

# dmesg | tail -n 20
[ 13452.123456] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: firmware error recovered
[ 13452.123789] RDMA: aborting QP 0xabc because state mismatch
```
Alex: RDMA firmware errors — suspicious. Could cause kernel-level packet drops. Which kernel and mlx driver version on nodepool-gpu-b nodes?
Priya: nodes on that pool are on kernel 5.15.0 and mlx5_core 5.3.0-1. nodepool-gpu-a (healthy) is on 5.15.0 + mlx5_core 5.2.x
Maria: Did kube-proxy mode change? ipvs proxier differences + mixed kernel/driver versions can make hashing inconsistent and cause uneven fanout.
Jordan: good call. Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` — asymmetric routing could be dropping return packets.
Priya: quick sysctls look standard. rp_filter=1. Running `kubectl get endpoints -o wide` shows endpoint lists are correct but traffic counters on some endpoints are ~40x others.
Priya: ```
# kubectl get endpoints model-serving -o yaml
subsets:
 - addresses:
   - ip: 10.2.5.21
   - ip: 10.2.5.22
   - ip: 10.3.7.19
 ports:
 - port: 443
``` 
Alex: Could be ipvs hashing choosing same backend more often due to different conntrack entries on nodes with RDMA NICs — they bypass some kernel paths.
Maria: Also check MTU on pod eth0 and host NIC. RDMA NICs often have lower MTU or offloads enabled that break GSO/TSO.
Priya: MTU on 10.2.5.x nodes = 1500, on 10.3.7.19 = 9000. ah. one node has jumbo frames enabled.
Jordan: there we go. MTU mismatch between endpoints will fragment packets or make kernel drop large segments leading to retries and retries amplify on hot endpoints.
Alex: That explains the 1200 tx count on 10.3.7.19 in ipvs stats — it's getting a lot of traffic (larger segments) and then timing out on returns.
Priya: I patched a quick workaround: reduced pod MTU on the jumbo node to 1500 and disabled RDMA offload for testing (`ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`). Observing reduced retries so far.
Maria: Nice. For a proper fix we should either standardize MTU across all GPU pools or add an iptables/MTU-preserve policy in CNI. Also evaluate kernel/firmware pins for mlx5.
Jordan: Action items:
- Priya: roll the temporary MTU/offs config to all problematic nodes and monitor (30m) :ambulance:
- Alex: open a firmware upgrade ticket with infra for mlx5 on nodepool-gpu-b and test on a canary (owner: Alex) :memo:
- Maria: add MTU check to cluster health & gating to prevent mixed MTU pools (owner: Maria) :gear:

Priya: rolled to two more nodes; error rate dropped ~85% on those backends. continuing to monitor.
Alex: I'll schedule firmware tests and coordinate with infra for a maintenance window.
Maria: I'll add an alert rule for endpoint fanout imbalance + MTU mismatch and a diagnostic runbook steps (kubectl endpoints, ipvsadm, ethtool, dmesg).
Priya: thanks all. marking P0 -> P1. Will update if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
